lines: {target}? Empty End stone gives no comfort.
Make sure travelers know this before visiting End Barrens. Keep away from edges and watch the sky.
The void makes silence feel heavier.
I will remember End Barrens as bare End land with nothing friendly in sight.
At the End barrens, which risk looked small until you were standing beside it?
A tired traveler can mistake any path for home. How did you avoid that near the End barrens?
Did anyone fall when End stone beside open void turned worse?
How long could you travel once still air with nowhere to hide set in?
I hope you filled every bottle before the End barrens. Did you?
That trip makes a day in my little boat sound gentle.
Did you pack enough to share, or only enough to survive the trip?
Did wet, heat, or grit damage anything you depended on?
I hope your shelter had one good wall and no surprises.
Which traveler surprised you by staying calm near the End barrens?
Could you smell the End barrens before it came into view?
What looked harmless near the End barrens until it began moving?
How many days passed before your legs forgave the journey?
Which mistake would you refuse to repeat near the End barrens?
You came back changed, though perhaps only you can name how.
Do you think the place would feel different on a second visit?
{target}? High End ground still ends in void.
Your best advice for End Highlands sounds simple. Mind bridges and do not chase anything floating.
Chorus fruit grows where falling is easy.
I'll remember End Highlands as high ground that does not feel safe.
The first bad moment at the End highlands must have changed the whole trip. What happened?
By the time you left the End highlands, did you know the way or merely know what to avoid?
A person watches enemies and forgets the ground. Did the End highlands punish that?
Did still air with nowhere to hide follow you on the return trip?
How carefully did you ration water on the way to the End highlands?
I would rather mend nets in rain than face endermen and the drop beyond the islands.
Did enough food for a longer return last until you were safely headed home?
What did you leave behind because carrying it home was not worth the risk?
Shelter found after dark rarely feels as safe as it looks. How was yours?
A good companion notices fear without making a speech about it. Who noticed yours?
When footsteps in all that silence changed, did you know why?
How near did the trouble come before anyone noticed it?
The return is where small injuries begin to matter. Who needed help?
Which lesson from that place belongs in every travel pack?
There is a part of that story you keep circling. You can leave it alone if you want.
If the choice were yours tomorrow, would you stay home?
{target}? Even the middle of the End feels lost.
I would tell anyone planning a trip to End Midlands one thing. Mark your way and distrust the horizon.
There is no village smell in that air.
I will remember End Midlands as End stone stretching where roads should be.
How quickly did trouble find you around the End midlands?
Did the route home feel easier to recognize after everything you had seen?
Was the ground at the End midlands harder on your legs or on your nerves?
Was there a safe place to wait out still air with nowhere to hide?
The road home feels different when the water is gone. How close did you come?
Give me rough water over endermen and the drop beyond the islands any day.
How many meals did the journey take beyond what you expected?
Of everything you packed, what earned its place?
How many people shared the safest resting place near the End midlands?
Someone must have kept you moving when home felt far away. Who was it?
Did the silence there feel peaceful, or did it feel watched?
When trouble reached the group, who spotted the safest opening?
What part of the return from the End midlands felt longest?
What rule kept you alive once the original plan failed?
Thank you for trusting me with the part that was hardest to say.
Was one journey to the End midlands enough for a lifetime?
{target}? Small islands feel smaller beside the void.
People setting out for Small End Islands should remember this. Bridge slowly and never look proud near an edge.
End stone gives no second chances below it.
I will remember Small End Islands as little bits of ground with forever around them.
Tell me when the small End islands stopped feeling like an adventure and started feeling dangerous.
On the way toward the small End islands, where did the route become difficult to read?
Could you move quickly over End stone beside open void, or did caution win?
At the small End islands, what sign told you the conditions were about to worsen?
Could you refill near the small End islands, or only ration what you carried?
There are days I complain about the lake. Today will not be one of them.
A hungry traveler makes quick mistakes. Did your food hold out?
A spare tool is dead weight until the first one fails. Which spare saved you?
How did you locate solid ground away from every edge when everyone needed rest?
Who remembered the plan when trouble scattered everyone?
Were there moments at the small End islands when hearing less felt worse?
Were you able to wait for danger to move, or did it force your hand?
Was the path home kinder than the one that took you out?
If you could change one choice from that trip, which would it be?
I can hear how tired you were, even now.
Tell that story by the fire sometime. Others need the honest version.
{target}? Victory there still feels far from home.
That warning belongs at the start of every trip to The End. Don't anger the tall ones and keep away from the void.
End stone does not smell like any living place.
I'll remember The End as a pale world with no proper village sound.
You made it back from the End. How close did that come to changing?
Did darkness change the route around the End more than you expected?
I would want both hands free on End stone beside open void. Did you manage that?
A hard journey feels longer in poor weather. How much longer did the End feel?
Tell me the truth about your supplies. How much water remained when you turned back?
I have crossed ugly water and still would not hurry toward the End.
The first hot bowl after the End must have settled more than hunger.
Did you carry one tool that turned out to matter more than all the rest?
Was rest possible once the sounds around the End started?
Who shared the watch with you when the End went quiet?
What was the first thing you heard after everyone stopped talking?
Which danger at the End deserves a clearer warning for the next traveler?
Home must have looked different after the End. What did you notice first?
Would better planning have changed the danger, or only your chances?
I was worried about the ending. I am glad you are here to tell it.
Who should hear this story before they make the same journey?
{target}? Nothing below is not the same as safety.
Tell the next traveler about The Void before they leave. Stay away from edges like they owe you emeralds.
There is no road back from falling forever.
I'll remember The Void as empty dark where even warnings feel small.
Did caution arrive before the danger at the void, or just after it?
What told you that you were still headed the right way at the void?
Which part of the void made you test every step before trusting it?
Did the weather near the void give you any warning before it changed?
Did anyone underestimate how much water the journey would take?
Water has frightened me before. I can hear that the void frightened you worse.
Which meal tasted best once you left the void behind?
What would you remove from the pack before another trip to the void?
What made a place feel safe enough to stop for the night?
Bad nights last longer alone. Who was awake with you?
What warning did the sounds around you give before you saw the danger?
Did you see any warning signs that only made sense afterward?
Did the weather follow you home from the void?
The next traveler needs the honest version. Where should the story begin?
That memory still has weight. Take your time with it.
After all that, is there anything near the void you still want to see?
